It is difficult to handle coherent multipaths in this methodology unless some additional processing is carried out. This article presents a novel methodology utilizing the direct data domain approach based on the spatial samples for the efficient computation of the adaptive weights in a phased array system. In this approach, the adaptive analysis is done on a snapshot-by-snapshot basis and therefore nonstationary environments can be handled quite easily including the coherent multipath environment. This is in contrast to conventional adaptive techniques where processing is done by taking the time averages as opposed to spatial averages. This approach is unlike the conventional statistical based techniques by eliminating the requirement of an interference covariance matrix and representing a rethinking of the entire conventional approach to adaptive processing. This approach provides greater flexibility in solving a wider class of problems at the expense of a slightly reduced number of degrees of freedom. Also in most adaptive processing the assumption that the target signal is coming from an exactly known direction will probably never be met in any real array. Or the adaptive array may be surveyed into location with small errors and thus the angle to the transmitter from the broadside of the array will be in error. Other applications of adaptive arrays will also have at least small errors in the direction of arrival of the desired signal. This article presents methodologies to treat this signal cancellation problem through the main beam constraints. Examples are presented to illustrate the applicability of this methodology to a wide class of problems. Finally, it is shown how to extend this methodology to two-dimensions, namely space-time adaptive processing (STAP). An example is presented to illustrate the detection of a saberliner tracked by an airborne forward looking radar in the presence of land, urban and sea-clutter.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from large transversely anisotropic inhomogeneous cylinders by FEM-FMA
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A hybrid solution of finite element method (FEM) and fast multipole algorithm (FMA) for transversely anisotropic inhomogeneous cylinders is presented. FMA is used to solve the integral equation to reduce the computation time and computer memory needs in electrically large objects and FEM to deal with anisotropic medium region. The accuracy and efficiency of the method are verified by numerical results.

articleTitle: An inexact Newton analysis of infinite nonlinearly loaded antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The inexact Newton approach and an infinite periodic structure Green's function including the array mutual coupling effects is presented to analyze the steady state scattering response of large nonlinearly loaded antenna array under multi-tones excitation. They are based on the method of moments, and then use the inexact Newton approach and an infinite periodic structure Green's function to solve the resulting equivalent circuit. The analysis is numerically efficient since it do not directly deal with the inverse Jacobian matrix and the array mutual coupling effect is included in an infinite periodic structure Green's function. Therefore, it is especially suitable for large periodic nonlinearly loaded antenna array under multi-tones excitation.

articleTitle: Pulse radiation antenna fed with a face-to-face TEM horn
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Greater interest in utilizing antenna systems for electromagnetic compatibility and target identification applications has been focused on the antenna's short pulse or ultrawideband (UWB) operation capabilities. One typical configuration for realizing a UWB antenna is to use a biconical TEM launcher as the feed to illuminate a parabolic reflector. However, the biconical TEM launcher has a greater aperture blockage. We introduce a novel antenna configuration with a modified face-to-face TEM horn feed. Generally, the face-to-face TEM horn will result in serious aperture blockage. To reduce the aperture blockage, quite a large part of the face-to-face horn is replaced by a metal wire frame. In practice, the modified feed consists of a mode convertor, a small TEM horn cascaded with a metal wire frame. The antenna is proven to be effective for high power subnanosecond pulse radiation.

articleTitle: Green's function for rough surface with Dirichlet, Neumann, and impedance boundary conditions
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical theory of rough surface Green's functions based on the extension of the diagram method of Bass and Fuks (1979), and Ito (1985) with the smoothing approximation used by Watson and Keller (1983, 1984). The method is a modification of the perturbation method and is applicable to rough surfaces with small RMS height. But the range of validity is considerably greater than the conventional perturbation solutions. We consider one-dimensional rough surfaces with Dirichlet, Neumann, and impedance boundary conditions. The coherent Green's function is obtained from the smoothed Dyson's equation by using a spatial Fourier transform. The mutual coherence function for the Green's function is obtained by the first-order iteration of the smoothing approximation applied to the Bethe-Salpeter equation in terms of a quadruple Fourier transform. These integrals are evaluated by the saddle-point technique. The equivalent bi-static cross section per unit length of the surface is compared to the conventional perturbation method and Watson-Keller's result. With respect to Watson-Keller's result, it should be noted that our result is reciprocal while the Watson-Keller result is nonreciprocal. Included in this paper is a discussion of the specific intensity at a given observation point. The theory developed will be useful for the RCS signature related problems and LGA (low grazing angle) scattering when both the transmitter and object are close to the surface.

articleTitle: Study for the automatic evaluation of co-site interference
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The evaluation of interference is one of the most important steps of radio spectrum management. It is also a method of reducing interference and dealing with the increasing rate of the spectrum utilization. Following the unceasing development of the communication, the need for an evaluation of the effect of interference on the spectrum usage is also growing. A direct effect of the spectrum resource constraint is the wastage of time for a man-made analysis of interference. With computer technology being widely available, the best method of eliminating this phenomenon is an automatic evaluation of interference. According to the standard GJB 3624-99 "methods for the evaluation of co-site interference", this paper researches and discusses the process of automatic interference evaluation.

articleTitle: Capacitances and inductances extraction for PCBs using exponential expansion method
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Based on Maxwell's equations, the mathematical formulation for the equivalent-circuit model of PCBs are discussed. A numerical methodology is presented for the extraction of capacitances and inductances of this model. The methodology combines the integral equation technique and the exponential expansion method. The exponential expansion method is employed for the evaluation of the scalar potential and the vector potential, resulting in a rapid and accurate extraction of the capacitances and inductances for PCBs.

articleTitle: Discrete analysis of a 3-dimensional airborne radome of superspheroidal shapes
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A discrete method or concept, which makes use of the spherical dyadic Green's functions (DGFs), is developed to study the electromagnetic transmission through an axis-symmetric radome of superspheroidal shapes. By means of the dyadic Green's functions, the discrete method inherently accounts for the curvature effects of the radome shell, which is generally ignored in classical approaches such as the ray-tracing method and the plane wave spectrum analysis. This proposed discrete method is thus able to give a more accurate analysis on the electromagnetic transmission problem through an airborne radome of superspheroidal shapes. Numerical results on power patterns and boresight errors are obtained and compared for various geometrical parameters of a superspheroidal radome.

articleTitle: Beamsteering optimized by appropriate random phasing quantization methods
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Beamsteering for a phased array is known to deviate from the desired pointing direction. This deviation occurs due to the use of digital phase shifters. In this correspondence, we develop the robust modification of the random phase quantization methods by means of appropriate random phasing quantization methods. For this purpose, the appropriate mean phase error equal-to-zero method (AMPEEZ), appropriate two probable value method (A2PV) and the appropriate phase-added method (APAM) are proposed.

articleTitle: Large signal analysis of on-chip interconnects using transport based approach
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A large signal analysis of on-chip interconnects is presented. A set of nonlinear equations combining the motion equations of charge carriers and Maxwell's equations is devised in the frequency domain for the fundamental mode and harmonics and then solved by the finite element method and Newton's iterations. This analysis provides knowledge of the field-carrier interaction, substrate nonlinearity and loss, slow-wave effect, etc. Numerical examples are provided for some practical material and geometrical parameters.

articleTitle: New expressions for equivalent edge currents
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: It is known that the results of the incremental length diffraction coefficients (ILDC) (Mitzner 1974) and the method of equivalent edge currents (MEC) (Michaeli 1984) differ by terms due to the physical optics (PO) current. These PO components become infinite for certain aspects of observation and illumination, by the extraction of the PO contribution from MEC. ILDC, unlike MEC, predicts finite currents for certain directions of observation. However, as already observed by Mitzner, ILDC also displays infinities for certain combinations of observation and incidence directions, though the range of singular aspects is reduced in comparison with MEC. Michaeli (1986) derived a set of expressions for the fringe current components of the equivalent edge currents, those expressions are finite for all aspects of illumination and observation, except for the Ufuntsev singularity. However, for certain non-singular aspects of the ILDC expressions, there is a wide divergence between Michaeli's (1986) results and Mitzner's results. In this paper, new expressions are derived for the fringe current components of equivalent edge currents, which are advantageous over those of Mitzner and Michaeli in both accuracy and versatility. A numerical example of the bistatic RCS of a square plate is given.

articleTitle: Comparison of time-domain responses of reflector and phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: This paper describes findings from a research program to investigate the main beam and sidelobe impulse responses of large phased array antennas and reflector antennas typically used for radar applications. Particular emphasis is given to the way that the impulse response changes from the main beam to the sidelobe region of the antenna. Antennas are designed to radiate a plane wave with a given polarization and frequency in a specified main beam direction. However, the time-domain impulse response will vary according to the actual implementation of the antenna design. Reflectors are designed to collimate a radiated beam by creating equal path delays and tend to have few parts. This produces a relatively simple and short time-domain impulse response. A phased array, on the other hand, generally collimates the beam by adjusting phases instead of path delays. In addition, there are more parts, which introduce multiple reflections. This gives the phased array a more complicated and longer impulse response than a reflector. These time-domain effects affect the transmit and received waveforms and therefore the advanced signal processing algorithms such as adaptive digital beamforming (ADBF) and space-time adaptive processing (STAP). Georgia Tech Research Institute (GTRI) has instituted an internal research program to investigate the time-domain phenomenology of phased array antennas and develop computer simulation tools and measurement capability for characterizing these phenomena. Some comparisons of a reflector antenna and a series corporate-fed phased array are presented.

articleTitle: Polarisation consideration in micro- and pico-cellular mobile communications
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: It has been proved, in this paper, that the average signal levels with vertical polarisation are higher than horizontal ones, by solving the diffraction field over multiple wedges, diffraction through symmetrical edges such as doorways or windows, and by experiments performed (at 5.3 GHz) in corridors. From the reflection and diffraction points of view, some useful conclusions have been obtained, which will be helpful in understanding the propagation mechanisms in mobile micro- and pico-cellular communications.

articleTitle: Internal problem for synthesis of antennas
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The directivity diagram (DD) for the horn antenna is defined by the amplitude and phase distribution (APD) of the field sources in the horn radiated angular opening. In turn, the APD is defined by the excitation and boundary conditions for the field on the horn walls. Theoretical and experimental investigations confirm the physical arguments about the possibility of the constructive iterative synthesis of the horn antennas, corresponding to the definite DD under limitations regarding the DD form. The general solution of this task as the inverse task of the radiation theory is quite difficult and does not have any practical importance, as it can quickly lead to the unrealistic sources AFD. Therefore we consider its solution by means of the detailed quantitative analysis of the waves high influence on the DD.

articleTitle: Approximate calculation method for window specification of antenna with medium cover
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: When an antenna with a medium cover is used, the window specification of the antenna must be determined in order to maintain its radiation characteristics. An approximate estimation can be made on the opening according to the calculation of the electromagnetic energy transmitted within the radiation cone of a dipole antenna. Such an estimation is comparatively accurate for directional antennas since a dipole radiator is semi-spherically isotropic while antennas of other types have radiation cones with a small radiation angle /spl theta//sub 0/ in characteristic. As an approximate method, it may be used to calculate the antenna's window specification, disregarding the pattern distortion induced by the window. Such a method is based on the calculation of the electromagnetic energy radiated by the antenna through the medium cover, whose thickness is d. Thus window specification of the antenna is determined to ensure that most part of the radiated electromagnetic energy can pass through the window.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from target buried in layer of randomly distributed trunks
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)

articleTitle: Designs for wide-band microstrip patch antenna for LMDS band
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: For the design and analysis of a patch antenna for the local multi-point distribution system (LMDS), we propose a special type of patch, which has a band along the outside of a rectangular patch. We minimize the electromagnetic emission from the fringing effect. As a consequence, we are able to increase the antenna efficiency and the frequency bandwidth. Compared with the rectangular patch antenna, the banded one has a wider bandwidth. The operating frequency bandwidth ranges from 24.5 GHz to 28.5 GHz and the VSWR is 2.0 using a Teflon substrate.

articleTitle: Bipolarized microwave antenna with a printed dipole feed
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A paraboloidal microwave antenna with a cross printed dipole as its feed is presented. It is characterized by bipolarization, simple construction, easy installation and so on.

articleTitle: The IMAGE mission and first observations from the radio plasma imager
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The Imager for Magnetopause-to-Aurora Global Exploration (IMAGE) mission is NASA's first satellite mission designed to image Earth's magnetosphere using remote sensing techniques. Extreme and far ultraviolet (EUV, FUV), energetic neutral atom (ENA), and radio plasma (RPI) imagers are mapping the aurora, the helium ions of the plasmasphere, the plasma sheet and polar cusp, and the total plasma distribution from the ionosphere to the magnetopause. IMAGE was launched on 25 March 2000 into an elliptical polar orbit with an altitude of 7 R/sub E/ at apogee and 1000 km at perigee. First observations obtained by RPI in the sounding and relaxation mode are reported.

articleTitle: FDTD analysis of the interaction between electromagnetic wave and inhomogenous anisotropic media
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: An efficient numerical FDTD repeated formulation has been devised for the study of anisotropic media. It can calculate the interior and exterior field of general anisotropic media. The formulations can be used in electromagnetic compatibility and bioelectromagnetic special effect of the interaction between electromagnetic waves and anisotropic media.

articleTitle: Study of the partially open cavity's resonant character
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Two methods are used to study the resonant character of a partially open cavity. They are the waveguide modal approach and the extended boundary integral method (BIM). Numerical experiments indicate that the far field contribution of the resonant modes in a cavity is zero. So no attention should be paid to these modes for far field calculation. Thus the difficulty of calculating cavities' far field radiation only relies on numerical instability of matrix inversion. This can be solved by SVD+BIM for the reason that singular value decomposition is a powerful and stable algorithm for dealing with matrices with very large condition number.

articleTitle: A robust tracking system for imaging radar altimeter
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The capability of precise range tracking is an important characteristic for an oceanic radar altimeter, different from other tracking radars. Up to now, however, all of the operational spaceborne radar altimeters can only be applied to the ocean because their tracking algorithms are based on an assumed echo model, and usually is Brown's (1977) model. But for the land case, we can not get a specified echo model, so the model-based tracking algorithm is not valid any longer. In this paper, we perform a study on a model-free tracking algorithm, i.e. the OCOG (offset center of gravity) algorithm. This is a robust tracking algorithm and is applied to an imaging altimeter, which is being researched. The imaging altimeter can be used both for ocean and land applications. The error characteristics of this algorithm are studied and a tracking simulation is given.

articleTitle: A study on composite scattering of targets and environment
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: An analysis of the composite scattering between the target and the environment is made. The two-dimensionally fractal function is used to model the rough surface, and the scattered electromagnetic field is calculated by using Kirchhoff's approximation. The validity of the result is assured by some reference, which indicates that the methods in this paper are reliable, then a simple and practical example is given.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis and comparison of frequency-domain electromagnetic system configurations
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The responses of electromagnetic (EM) systems in the frequency-domain depend on the transmitting frequency and configuration between the transmitter and receiver under certain geological environments. In order to reduce the noise from the primary field for improving the sensitivity of the EM system, special techniques have to be employed. A sound analysis for the coil configurations can help the EM system design. This paper addresses the theoretical sensitivity analysis of coil configuration EM systems. By analysis and comparison, we see that the null configurations can also receive the second field generated by the three-dimensional targets located in the shallow subsurface. This configuration is less sensitive to the geometric setting errors than the perpendicular configuration is. These characteristics can be applied to simplify the high-frequency EM system design for near-surface applications. Test results show that the null configuration is sensitive to image small three-dimension targets located in the shallow subsurface even though the residual primary field is not cancelled.

articleTitle: A new method based on elliptic cylindrical wave function for large aspect ratios scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The original T-matrix method cannot be available to determine the scattering field under the condition of a large aspect ratio scattering body of resonant mode. In this paper, a T-matrix method (called the extended T-matrix method) which is based on the elliptic cylindrical wave function is proposed for the two-dimensional scattering problems.

articleTitle: Auxiliary functions in electromagnetic theory
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this paper, all auxiliary functions in electromagnetic (EM) theory are discussed, and the author points out that some inherent relationships exist among them. We observe that these functions are not isolated from each other, and the scalar wave functions are the most important. The transforms between any two scalar wave functions are very useful for solving EM boundary problems.

articleTitle: Numerical diffraction coefficients of the irregular edge on a semi-infinite conductive circular-cylinder-a GMT/PO approach
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In the problem of the electromagnetic scattering, the conductive surface of electrically large objects with complex geometry can be divided into a number of sub-surfaces with simple shape far each. The total scattering field may be considered as summation of the physical optics (PO) from all sub-surfaces, but the additional diffracted contribution from the discontinuous junction between those sub-surfaces must be taken into account. Besides the asymptotic expression of diffraction coefficients had been derived for the regular edge of canonical scatterer, only the numerical diffraction coefficients (NDC) can be employed. A hybrid method of the generalized multi-pole technique and physical optics (GMT/PO) was developed previously for extracting the NDC of an irregular conductive wedge. In this paper, the GMT/PO hybrid method accompanied with an iteration technique is extended to extract 3-D NDC from an an irregular edge between the terminal cross-section and the circularly cylindrical surface of a semi-infinite conductive scatterer. The computed RCS (backward NDC) of a finite circular-cylinder with regular edge are in good agreement with the measured data.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor integrating system propagation research
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A very useful multi-sensor airborne surveying system of real time data processing and transmission is being developed. The sensors of the surveying system consist of remote sensing instruments. The processed and compressed data are transmitted to the satellite, and then the receivers on the ground receive the data from the satellite and process and display them. Because of its advantages the Ku-frequency band is used. But the satellite-to-ground path attenuation is very serious because of rain, heavy cloud or other factors. In order to compensate the path attenuation, we have conducted propagation investigations and developed an uplink power control method for the airborne-satellite path.

articleTitle: On the application of the analytical continuation from real to complex spaces to some EM field solutions
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The analytical continuation from the real to the complex space is a mathematical tool which appears to be very interesting applied to EM problems. We look at the main restrictions associated to some common solutions and analyze certain rules which should be taken into account in order to apply these methods. Through some examples, we illustrate how new field solutions or alternative formulations may be obtained.

articleTitle: A two dimensional study on reflections from a plasma flame
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The advantage of using a plasma sheet as a reflector for EM waves is in obtaining an EM controlled fast steering beam. In many cases, however, the easiest way to generate a plasma sheet is to have a plasma gun and shooting into a vacuum chamber. The distribution of the plasma is then not a uniformly distributed sheet but a flame-like distribution. In this paper, a preliminary discussion is given of the reflections of EM waves from a flame-like plasma sheet (2D case). This may give some basic understanding for the design of this kind of reflector.

articleTitle: A finite-element analysis of electromagnetic field produced by ELF sources enclosed by a nonlinear ferromagnetic pipe
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The electromagnetic field produced by extremely-low-frequency (ELF) sources within a nonlinear ferromagnetic pipe is of practical interest especially for underground power cables. We present a finite element analysis for determining the electromagnetic field everywhere generated by ELF sources enclosed by a nonlinear ferromagnetic pipe, using an underground pipe-type cable as example. The finite-element method is employed to compute the potentials and fields in the interior region. The information on the potentials and fields obtained can be used to determine the cable parameters of practical interest, such as the zero-sequence impedance. In the finite-element solution, special attention is paid to the nonlinear B-H characteristics of the pipe, and an iterative procedure is employed to determine the varying permeability of the pipe. Then, to determine the fields in the region exterior to the pipe, we employ the equivalence principle to formulate a model equivalent to the exterior region. In the equivalent model, the equivalent surface currents can be obtained directly from knowledge of the fields on the outer surface of the pipe as the finite-element solutions. Using the equivalent surface currents, the magnetic field outside the pipe is computed.

articleTitle: A near-field diagnostic technique based on equivalent magnetic currents
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A new technique is presented for determining the amplitude and phase distribution over the aperture of the antenna under test from planar near-field measurements. The main computational formulae are provided and proven to be accurate and effective by use of the detailed numerical simulation compared with the related literature and an experiment.

articleTitle: Extension of the Kennaugh null theory
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In radar polarimetry, Kennaugh (1952) first introduced the concept of the characteristic polarization states. This paper introduced the concepts of the co-null and the co-null Abelian group for extending the Kennaugh null theory to the case of two independent polarization states. For two arbitrary targets, it is proved that there exists one pair of polarization states such that the received powers of both targets equal zero. This polarization states' pair is called the co-null of the two targets, which can easily be obtained by solving an eigenvalue problem. Based on group theory, another concept- the co-null Abelian group is introduced for the symmetric scattering matrix case, and many important results are presented: e.g., the relations between the co-null and the co-pol/X-pol nulls, the structure of the co-null Abelian group, and the relations between the co-null Abelian group and two classes of targets: symmetric targets and H-targets. Finally, the co-null for the asymmetric scattering matrix case is studied. The concepts of the mono-co-null Abelian group and the bi-co-null Abelian group are introduced, and the relations between both groups are presented.

articleTitle: Transient excitation of special slotted bicone
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The nonstationary Green's functions boundary problem for a perfectly conducting bicone consisting of a cone with periodical longitudinal slots and an isotropic one is considered. This geometry can be regarded as a model of special biconical slotted antennas and reflectors. The solution method employs the Laplace transforms, the Kontorovich-Lebedev integral transforms and the Riemann-Hilbert method.

articleTitle: Investigations of the high-latitude ionosphere using imaging riometer at Zhongshan Station, Antarctica
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: An imaging riometer with an 8/spl times/8 antenna array was installed at Zhongshan Station, Antarctica in January 1997. The structure and working principle of the instrument are described. The imaging riometer technique has proved a valuable tool for investigations of the high-latitude ionospheric disturbances. To illustrate the potential of the new technique, this paper discusses the observations at cusp latitudes of sudden cosmic noise absorption events, polar cap absorption (PCA) events and a typical midnight absorption.

articleTitle: Deducing high-frequency Doppler shift from vertical measuring data
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A formula is provided for calculating the phase track and the Doppler frequency shift based on the measured frequency-height diagram. As an example, the Doppler effect for a 10 MHz standard electronic wave in the Xi'an-Dalian link at sunrise was calculated and analyzed.

articleTitle: The study of the characteristics of horizontal gradient of ionospheric electron concentration at Chongqing
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The electron concentration horizontal gradient vector of the ionosphere and its south-north and east-west components over Chongqing station are analyzed and calculated in this paper, using the first approximation, time correlation and space correlation and another approach introduced in this paper. And then, the validity of the two methods is analyzed and compared.

articleTitle: A new type of broadband printed antenna
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A new type of broadband printed antenna is proposed. The current distribution and input impedance are obtained by the method of moments with integral equations. Comparison with experimental results shows good agreement. The results indicate that the bandwidth of the new antenna is much larger than normal microstrip dipole fabricated in the same substrate. A bandwidth greater than 10% can also be obtained on thin substrates (h<0.01/spl lambda//sub 0/). The new antenna is low cost, simple, and easily integrated with MMIC.

articleTitle: Dyadic Green's function for an unbounded anisotropic medium in cylindrical coordinates
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The dyadic Green's function for an unbounded anisotropic medium is treated analytically in the Fourier domain. The Green's function is initially expressed as a triple Fourier integral, which is then reduced to a double one by performing the integration over the longitudinal Fourier variable. The singular behavior of the Green's dyadic as the observation point traverses the source point is discussed for the anisotropic case.

articleTitle: Feasibility analysis and practice of super-long distance microwave transmission between islands
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Strong sea-surface reflection and weather changes pose great difficulties for microwave transmission, especially over long interstation distances. Through a successful construction of microwave stations which stand 80 km apart, combined with analysis of transmission mechanisms and observations of attenuation and refraction of microwaves over sea surfaces, it is demonstrated that stable and reliable transmission can be obtained without using diversity spacing. Methods of selecting the most suitable way for transmission are also discussed.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Kirchoff model and the IEM model for rough surface scattering using numerical simulation
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The validity of the Kirchhoff approximation and IEM model for rough perfect conducting surface scattering is examined by comparison with simulation results obtained by solving integral equations. First, the surface current and scattered field of approximation for surfaces with different surface length, different root-mean-square surface height and wavelength is compared with solving integral equations. Then, the scattering coefficients calculated from the approximation and Monte Carlo simulation are compared.

articleTitle: Duality of the IE-MEI method and its application to 2-D perfect conducting scatterers
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: We show that an integral equation formulation of the measured equation of invariance (IE-MEI) fulfils a duality and the duality is useful to solve the scattering problems of a 2-D object for TM and TE waves incident simultaneously. The duality of the IE-MEI is derived naturally from the formulation of the IE-MEI. From the formulation, we have found that the application range of the IE-MEI method is very wide: it can treat scattering problems for perfect electric conductors (PEC), lossy materials and lossless materials. The excitation source can be near or far from the scatterer. In the IE-MEI method, there exists an efficient computational algorithm using sparse matrices. We show the validity of the algorithm by numerical examples of a circular and a square PEC cylinders illuminated by a TM and a TE plane waves.

articleTitle: Design method and application of multi-mode corrugated horn
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: This paper presents the design method of a multi-mode conical corrugated horn which aims to utilize the unwanted mode (EH/sub 12/ mode) but not to restrain it, which can be used for the design of a wideband (or multi-band) corrugated horn. The designed horn has good radiation characteristics, where the maximum cross-polarization is below -30 dB over the band range from 3.4 GHz to 6.65 GHz.

articleTitle: Discrete time-domain analysis of nonuniform lossless coupled transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: We present a discrete time-domain method for transient analysis of multiple coupled nonuniform lossless transmission lines. The method of the solution is based on the steplines approximation and modal decomposition method.

articleTitle: Active characteristics of lineaments in central province Shandong and their control to earthquakes
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this paper, using macroscopic features, integrative features of images, the characteristics of multi-temporal data and image processing, the author interprets the image features of the Yi-shu fault zone. The author analyses the activity features of the lineaments combined with physical exploration, earthquake data and the regional stress field, then discusses the relationship of the lineament activity and earthquakes and points to the activity of Yi-shu fault zone as a cause of the appearance and activity of 2 groups of faults, NW trending and near NS trending. Their intersection is related to volcanic eruptions and earthquake origin.

articleTitle: Radar image simulation from fully polarimetric scattering of heterogeneous canopy surface
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Polarimetric imagery of high resolution SAR is one of most important advances in microwave remote sensing. This paper, using the fully polarimetric Mueller matrix solution and ray tracing method, simulates radar images for fully polarimetric scattering from a heterogeneous canopy surface. Non-uniform 3D structures and non-uniform distribution of the multi-components of the surface canopy are taken into account. Simulated image texture demonstrates the spatial variation of the radar echoes due to canopy 3D-heterogeneity, and is also compared with an AirSAR image in the P,L,C bands.

articleTitle: The retrieval of oceanic wind field using the pencil-beam conical scanning scatterometer
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: An algorithm for retrieving the near surface oceanic wind field using the pencil-beam conical scanning scatterometer was developed. The pencil-beam conical scanning scatterometer is one mode of the China spaceborne multi-mode microwave sensors. Our simulations show that for the cell at different azimuthal position, the retrieval accuracy is different for the same measurement deviation. Finally, a helicopter experiment for backscattering model development has been introduced and preliminary results have been given.

articleTitle: Wide-band microstrip patch antenna design for LMDS band
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: There has been a constant effort to study methods for increasing the bandwidth of microstrip antennas. In this paper, we propose a special type of the external rectangular patch, for the design and analysis of an antenna using a local multipoint distribution system (LMDS). We minimized electromagnetic emissions from the fringing effect. As a result, we obtained an increase in antenna efficiency and frequency bandwidth. We were also able to design the wideband antenna easily, because of the difference in parameter between the aimed and the simulated antenna was reduced greatly. In comparison with the rectangular patch antenna, the banded one has a wider bandwidth. We set the operation frequency bandwidth from 24.5 GHz to 28.5 GHz on the basis of the operation frequency band at VSWR 2.0, and used a Teflon substrate with relative dielectric ratio is 2.6.

articleTitle: Mysterious behavior of the excited near fields on printed-circuit transmission lines: physical contribution of a non-physical solution
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: It is well known that, when most printed-circuit transmission lines are excited by a practical monochromatic high-frequency source, the near-field amplitude decay exponentially along the line axis due to the excitation of a leaky mode. Such a situation usually occurs when the leaky mode is the only physical solution at a given frequency. However, we sometimes meet with an unexpected situation in which the near-field amplitude decays with a decay constant much smaller than that expected from the leaky-mode eigenvalue, even though the only physical solution at the operating frequency is the leaky-mode solution. No answer to this mysterious situation could be found previously, until when we found that such a slow decay in the near-field-amplitude variation depends strongly on an indirect effect from a nonphysical improper-real solution that exists at the operating frequency. We show several kinds of evidence that prove our interpretation of this mysterious problem, including theoretical discussions and experimental results.

articleTitle: The response of a rotative two wire transmission line excited by external electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The induced currents in the terminals of the terminated two-wire rotative transmission line, excited by external nonuniform electromagnetic field are obtained in time domain.

articleTitle: The design of the feed for a microwave relay antenna system with super high performance
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The optimum design of the feed for a C-band microwave relay antenna with super high performance is achieved by using high frequency structure simulation. By means of the perturbation method of the structure sizes, the manufacturing tolerance of critical sizes for the feed are determined. The agreement between the measured and computed data is excellent. The measured VSWR and isolation of the feed are better than 1.06 and 40 dB in the range of 4.4-5.0 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: FD-TD for dispersive media with parameters known in limited frequency range
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this paper the frequency-dependent time domain (FDTD) method is applied to the problem of the known parameters of dispersive media in a limited frequency range. Conclusions are drawn from the analysis.

articleTitle: Calculating the cutoff frequencies of heteromophic waveguide by operator theory
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The cutoff frequencies of heteromophic waveguide in a special structure is solved with the matching of the electric and magnetic field on the virtual boundary by partial differential operator theory. The method can be used to not only for solving the cutoff frequencies of almost all modes precisely and expediently, but also for calculating the transmitting characteristics of a ridged waveguide and the other heteromophic waveguide loaded by a rectangular metal.

articleTitle: The reducing technique for dealing with electromagnetic scattering problems of single axis symmetric structure
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: By introducing an image scattering source, a new formulation based on the method of moments (MoM) is proposed. With this formulation, three-quarters of the calculation time and half of the computer storage can be saved in computer calculation.

articleTitle: The optimum designing method for wide bandwidth meander-line circular polarizer
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The basic theory of the multilayer meander-line circular polarizer is presented. Both the Floquet series and the algebraic analyzing methods are given, meanwhile the improprieties in some papers are also pointed out. With the application of microwave network theory, the calculating method for parameters such as axis ratio and insert loss is given. By utilizing the multi-object optimum method, the designing method for meander-line circular polarizer with a bandwidth of 6-18 GHz is presented.

articleTitle: Dyadic Green's function for biaxial medium
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In the Fourier domain, the dyadic Green's function is initially expressed as a triple Fourier integral, and next reduced to a double one by performing the integration over the longitudinal Fourier variable for an unbounded biaxial medium. A delta-type source term is extracted, which is dependent on the particular coordinate system.

articleTitle: A novel phased array antenna of multiple object tracking radar
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The multiple object tracking radar was put in operation in November, 1999. As one of the important radar subsystems, the phased array antenna system displayed good tactical properties and featured a high antenna gain and low cross-polarization (antenna efficiency /spl ges/31%, circular polarization axial ratio <1 dB). Its one-degree pencil beam can be positioned with high accuracy to any point within the array's cone scan coverage. Some important antenna parameters are listed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from a conducting target surrounded by fractal atmospheric turbulence
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this paper, the theory of electromagnetic wave scattering from a conducting target surrounded by fractal atmospheric turbulence is presented. The first and second order moments of the scattering fields are derived by considering the effects of the fractal atmospheric turbulence. The relationships between the mutual coherence function, structure function and fractal dimension are given for plane wave and spherical wave incidence, respectively. The normalized backscattering radar cross section /spl sigma//sub n/ of a perfectly conducting disk is calculated. It is shown that the influence of fractal dimension on /spl sigma//sub n/ is obvious for atmospheric turbulence with a fractal spectrum distribution.

articleTitle: An extrapolation technique for antenna and RCS analysis involving large bodies
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Summary form only given. The objectives of this paper are twofold. First we present a technique, based on the reciprocity principle, for computing the patterns of antennas located on large structures. Towards this end we utilizing the technique based on the fast multipole method (FMM), which enables us to handle problems that require tens of thousands of unknowns in the context of the method of moments. The FMM makes it possible for us to get to the lower edge of the high frequency regime, where the currents on the body begin to exhibit certain asymptotic characteristics when it is illuminated by a plane wave. We take advantage of this behavior of the currents to extrapolate them to higher frequencies for which the problem becomes too large to be handled, even by using the FMM. We illustrate the application of this approach by considering slot antennas mounted on cylindrical structures, and show how the pattern extrapolation for this type of problem is carried out. The second part of the paper also deals with the extrapolation approach, but for RCS computations. We show, once again, that the bistatic RCS of targets with multiple edges and corners can be tracked as a function of the frequency for a given combination of incident and observation angles to generate a representation for the scattered field that can be extrapolated to higher frequencies. Thus problems that are too large to handle by conventional numerical techniques now become tractable, once this representation covering the resonance region and the lower end of the high frequency range can be found. Towards this end we employ a combination of the generalized pencil of function (GPOF) method and the genetic algorithm (GA) to derive a finite series of complex exponentials, whose coefficients and exponents are both functions of frequency. This representation is initially matched over a certain frequency range, whose upper limit is the highest frequency for which the given problem is numerically tractable. Once a good match has been established, it is relatively straightforward to carry out an extrapolation of the frequency response to as high a frequency as is desired. The paper concludes with a discussion of the scope and limitations of the proposed extrapolation approach for solving high frequency scattering and radiation problems.

articleTitle: Research on the adaptive array in CDMA system
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this paper, three categories of adaptive antennas are compared and we pay attention to the direction-finding adaptive antenna. To improve the performance of the direction-finding adaptive antenna, the geometry of the array is optimized, and a kind of concentric-ring antenna array is utilized to suppress the co-channel interference in a given cell. The performance of this kind of adaptive antenna is analyzed simultaneously.

articleTitle: A note on dyadic Green's function of electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: This paper gives electromagnetic wave field and irrotational field with proper degrees of freedom and the simplified expressions of dyadic Green's functions correspondence to electromagnetic wave field and irrotational field is deduced respectively.

articleTitle: Determining the specification of antenna window on medium cover
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A method to determining the window specification of antennas with medium cover is presented. Medium cover is used widely to deduce the back scattering of antenna. But the medium always influences the radiation characteristics of the antenna. To guarantee the radiation characteristic of antennas with medium cover, it is important to open an aperture on the medium cover, which is called the antenna window. The method presented here can determine the minimal specification of the window. The result indicates that the antenna window affects the antenna RCS greatly.

articleTitle: Development of a 3-D GPR simulator using the FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The Monte Carlo method is used to simulate the electromagnetic scattering from a target buried in a layer of randomly distributed trunks. Using the moment method checks the validity of the second-order scattering field (interaction of target-trunk pairs). An iterative algorithm and spherical vector wave function are used to calculate the scattering matrix of the finite-length multi-layer dielectric cylinder and target (sphere) respectively. Finally, the influences of the bark layer and the roughness of the surface on the scattering pattern of the target (sphere) are discussed for the L band, C band and X band. Because of the effect of random media such as trunks, the scattering coefficients for the target become smaller. The low frequency can be used for the purpose of target detection and recognition buried in random media. The present work provides a theoretical basis for the simulated scattering from targets buried in forest canopies including the effects of multiple scattering.

articleTitle: Reduction of electromagnetic radiation using conducting wires or multilamina shielding
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Shielding telecommunication, electronic and mobile systems from undesired electromagnetic radiation is a problem of great interest. The objective of a modelling work is to have the optimal solution with the least cost giving the most perfect isolation on a wide frequency band. Two solutions are developed. The first consists of isolation using crossed lines and the second consists of isolation using multilamina shielding. The propagation through each is discussed. A comparison is based on the criteria of optimisation of the shielding effectiveness in each case. Generally, these solutions are easy to achieve and can be used to reduce the electromagnetic perturbation in telecommunication systems.

articleTitle: Pulsed beam propagation in dispersive media
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the behavior of transient wavefields due to a pulsed-beam (PB) wavepacket launched obliquely from a hypothetical aperture plane in a medium with generic dispersion k(w), where k and w are wavenumber and frequency, respectively. The problem is solved through spectral decomposition into plane waves in the frequency (w) and spatial wavenumber (/spl xi/) domains, followed by asymptotics on the spectral inversion integrals, with w-synthesis performed before /spl xi/-synthesis. Special attention in the transient spectral domain is given to paraxial PB approximations and to criteria for their range of validity. The resulting PBs can be used to synthesize transient wavefields excited by arbitrary space-time source distributions of finite support on a specified aperture plane in the medium.

articleTitle: Computer-aided design of four wire dual-mode spiral antenna
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A dual-mode broadband antenna specially designed to simultaneously provide low and high angle radiation patterns within a bandwidth of 5 to 30 MHz relative to a horizontal ground plane is described. This particular antenna utilizes four wire radiators in the form of an inverted conical log-spiral supported in a vertically extending fashion a predetermined distance above the horizontal ground plane. The spiral antenna is theoretically analyzed and its current integral equation is given. For purposes of computer aided design of the spiral antenna, numerical calculation is applied using Galerkin's method. Finally, the numerical results are given and discussed.

articleTitle: An anisotropic PML absorbing boundary condition using for waves propagating in dispersive medium
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this paper, an anisotropic perfectly matched layer (PML) absorbing boundary condition is presented for the finite difference-time domain (FDTD) method to simulate waves propagating in a dispersive medium. Numerical results show that by properly choosing the constitutive parameters of the anisotropic PML, the method provides a nearly reflectionless absorbing boundary and it is an effective method in the simulation of waves propagating in a dispersive medium.

articleTitle: A novel cost function of adaptive antenna for CDMA system
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Conventional adaptive antennas optimize the base band spreading signal; the cost function is the mean square error of the difference between the weighted spreading signals and a reference. The cost function does not utilize the merits of CDMA that spread spectrum technology can improve the signal SNR. The article presents a new cost function which optimizes the despreading signals of the base band element outputs, and is the mean square error of the difference between the despreading signal and a new reference signal. Computer simulations has been further carried out, and the results illustrate that the novel cost function can improve the system capacity.

articleTitle: Experimental studies on GPR velocity estimation and imaging method using migration in frequency-wavenumber domain
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Similar to migration in the (k/sub x/, /spl omega/) domain of seismic techniques, this paper presents a approach to focus on ground-penetrating radar (GPR) data and estimate the electromagnetic wave velocity underground. To demonstrate the validity and feasibility of this approach, experimental GPR data are conducted with an object buried in two different kinds medium. It is found that in a homogeneous medium, this approach can be used to estimate the electromagnetic wave velocity underground and improve the imaging resolution.

articleTitle: A new numerical scheme to obtain the RCS of three-dimension bodies using PSTD algorithm
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: A new numerical method, the pseudospectral time domain (PSTD) algorithm with an infinite order of accuracy and high efficiency, is used to obtain the RCS of a three-dimensional object. In implementation of the PSTD, the incident plane wave pulse is simulated with an initial-condition excitation technique based on a pair of one-dimensional PSTD update equations to eliminate the unwanted Gibbs phenomenon. The pure scattered field formulation is utilized to surmount the difficulty of introducing the incident field into computational space. A PSTD near-to-far zone field transform is developed for the analysis of RCS. Numerical results presented in this work confirm the efficacy of the PSTD method.

articleTitle: A solution to inhomogeneous 3D railgun
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In a railgun, which is used to accelerate objects, electrical energy is used to drive the system. In order to reach hypervelocity, a power supply with an immense amount of energy must be used which causes an extra ordinary current on the rail and the armature. This current makes thermal energy by ohmic attenuation and warms up various points and therefore changes the electrical, thermal and mechanical specifications of the structure. This paper presents a method by which one can consider the inhomogeneity created by temperature changes along the structure. In this method, the instantaneous current distribution in the structure and the heat caused by it are calculated, and then the temperature distribution is obtained. The electrical conductivity (/spl sigma/), thermal conductivity (k) and specific heat (c) are considered to be inhomogeneous and are calculated at every instant until the specifications of the material forming the structure can be corrected at any instant. A three dimensional finite element method with nonuniform meshing at any instant is used.

articleTitle: Sea clutter measurement on the Yellow Sea using an instrumentation radar
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In a maritime environment, sea clutter is one of the most important factors to be considered in operating radars. It is difficult to describe the characteristics of sea clutter as a simple model because sea clutter is dependent on each radar system and many other environmental parameters. Usually an expensive special system is used to obtain sea clutter data. However, we tried to acquire the sea clutter data using an instrumentation radar, AN/TPQ-39 with some additional equipment. The data were acquired on the Yellow Sea, with varying grazing angles at a few sea states. The results showed that the amplitude statistics of the observed sea clutter fit into the Weibull distribution well. We also proposed a simplified model for the backscattering coefficient of sea clutter on the Yellow Sea at X-band.

articleTitle: Analyzing infra-acoustic wave disturbance-observed by our Doppler detector in typhoon season
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this article, using two typical cases we point out that in China there exists an F2 layer infra-acoustic wave disturbance, concerning which we found three remarkable spectral peaks due to severe weather.

articleTitle: An ultra wide band test system to test the transient electric fields and magnetic fields generated by electrostatic discharge (ESD)
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: An ultra wide band test system consisted of a custom ultra-wide band E-field antenna and H-field antenna with wide band oscilloscope and VXI systems were used to test the transient electromagnetic field generated by an electrostatic discharge (ESD). Many tests were carried out on a real charged human body discharging to the ground. The results show that the electric field at a distance of 10 cm from a human holding a metal pen with a potential of 2 kV discharging to ground is 410 V/m and the magnetic field is 28 A/m at a distance of 3 cm from the discharge. The band of the field is extremely wide, ranging from several MHz to above 1 GHz. An electrostatic discharge is also one of the most common harmful electromagnetic sources for electronic equipment.

articleTitle: A efficient mixed algorithm of L-MEI and DDM for the wave scattering by a cylinder
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this paper a localized MEI (measured equation of invariance) method (L-MEI) is developed and combined with the domain decomposition method (DDM) (Yin and Hong 1999) for the simulation of scattering by a cylinder. In L-MEI, the whole domain of solution is decomposed into many subdomains. Different from the conventional MEI method, the MEI coefficients of the L-MEI method in each subdomain are only dependent of the localized metrons that are defined in the subdomain. The localization of the MEI coefficients has some advantages: (1) speeding up the calculation of the MET coefficients and saving memory costs, (2) making the MEI method available for more complex structures, and (3) obtaining a band sparse matrix without changing the order of the nodes.

articleTitle: Nonlinear model and readback distortions of MR head
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: Magnetoresistive (MR) heads have been widely used in high density magnetic recording systems. The MR head non-linearity degrades the detection performance. A 3rd-order polynomial model is used to characterize the MR head non-linearity. With the extracted dipulse method, the readback distortions of the MR head are investigated through simulation. Some simulation results are given.

articleTitle: Numerical diffraction coefficients of the irregular top on a conductive cone-a GMT/PO approach
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In the electromagnetic scattering problem, the total scattering field of electrically large objects with complex geometry may be considered as a summation of the physical optics (PO) from all smooth sub-surfaces and the additional diffracted contribution from the discontinuous junction between those sub-surfaces. In order to calculate the results exactly the diffraction coefficients are the key, but only several canonical scatterers, such as the wedge, have an asymptotic expression of the diffraction coefficients. So, the numerical diffraction coefficients (NDC) of most scatters must be studied. Some 2-D NDC had been reported, and a hybrid method of the generalized multi-pole technique and physical optics (GMT/PO) was developed for extracting the 2-D and then 3-D NDC of an irregular conductive wedge. In this paper, the GMT/PO hybrid method accompanied with the iteration technique is extended to extract 3-D NDC from irregular top of the semi-infinite conductive cone. The computed backward radar cross sections (RCS) of a finite cone with a regular top are in good agreement with the results obtained by the geometrical diffraction method (GTD).

articleTitle: Identifying radar secondary data for signal detection
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In signal detection, one is interested in the problem of detection of a given radar signal s which is a complex vector in the presence of noise in transmission. The signal may be a set of voltages that an EM wave from the selected search directions induces on a number of receiving elements. The actual observed data Y may be a pure noise vector n or the signal s plus a noise vector n. It is assumed that the noise follows a complex multivariate normal distribution with mean O and covariance matrix /spl Sigma/. Statistically, the model can be described as Y=s+n where s is a specific signal and n is a noise random vector. The goal is to test the null hypothesis that Y=n versus the alternative hypothesis that Y=s+n. Reed et al. (1974) discussed an adaptive procedure for the above detection problem in which two sets of input data are used, which are called the primary and secondary data. A radar receives primary data Y/sub 0/ which may or may not contain a signal, and secondary data Y/sub 1/,Y/sub 2/,...,Y/sub n/ which are assumed to contain only noise, independent of and statistically identical to the noise components of the primary data. The goal is to test H/sub 0/:/spl mu/=O versus H/sub 1/:/spl mu/=s where /spl mu/ is the population mean of Y/sub 0/. Kelly (1986) used the likelihood ratio principle to derive a test statistic for the above hypothesis testing problem. Chen and Wicks (1999) proposed a selection procedure which compares the covariance matrices of the secondary data with that of the primary data. It is used to identify and eliminate those observations that have a different covariance structure from the secondary data. It retains homogeneous radar data for further investigation. As described in Chen and Wicks (1999), this procedure can be applied prior to the step of estimating the covariance matrix of the secondary data in Kelly (1986). The selection procedure is discussed together with a simulation study.

articleTitle: Recursive reduction techniques for wave scattering by complex structures
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave scattering by a system of complex structures, formed as a mixture of conductors and inhomogeneous dielectric material, is reduced, recursively, to a surface integral equation in terms of only electric current distributed over the outermost surface of each complex body. Numerical results are obtained for the case of TM wave scattering by a foil-backed dielectric cylinder.

articleTitle: The computing model of radiation pattern for imperfect radome
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: In this paper a computed model for the radiation pattern of an imperfect radome is given. Based on the model a formula is derived and the computed results are given to explain the effects of an imperfection of the radome on the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: On classification and symmetrical relations of electromagnetic dyadic Green functions
publicationTitle: 2000 5th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation, and EM Theory. ISAPE 2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX417)
abstract: The classification and symmetrical relations of electromagnetic Green functions are summarized. As well as a fact that there is no symmetrical relation generally for third kind Green function of magnetic type is pointed out. Some suggestions about these two problems mentioned above in the title for teaching are provided.
